newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Avalon Oil says seeks AIM listing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Avalon Oil says seeks AIM listing.

text.p: U.S.-based exploration and production company Avalon Oil said on Monday that it planned to seek a listing on the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) in order to fund a joint venture with Russia's Gazprom.

In a statement the company said proceeds from the placing would be used to fund a 49 percent stake in Stimul, a joint venture company formed to undertake exploration and production in Orenburg, southern Russia.
The remainder of Stimul would be controlled by Orenburggazprom, a subsidiary of RAO Gazprom, one of the world's largest producers of natural gas.
Sources close to Avalon told Reuters the company hoped to raise around 35 million stg from the AIM listing, giving it a market capitalization of around 80 million stg.
Marketing of the issue is due to start this month, with a listing possible in March.
Henderson Crosthwaite Corporate Finance and Henderson Crosthwaite Institutional Brokers Ltd have been appointed as advisers to Avalon.

Avalon, which is based in Oklahoma, said Stimul had been granted a license to develop and produce proven and probable oil reserves of 371 million barrels at the eastern end of the 65-mile long Orenburg field, which has gas reserves of around 70 trillion cubic feet.

Avalon said current production at the site was around 2,850 barrels per day. The U.S. company plans to introduce modern technology and exploitation techniqes to boost this to an average of 18,500 barrels per day in 1998.
The two partners intend to increase the share capital of Stimul to around $101 million from just $1 million.

Avalon Oil chairman John Wieczorek said the placing would "help fund the provision of advanced western drilling techniques, previously unavailable to Gazprom, which will be used to develop the significant proven oil reserves of the Orenbug field.
Without Avalon's expertise he added that it "would not be possible to exploit this field economically."
